verdict.rationale: CockroachDB's first-party docs describe a native `VECTOR` type that is compatible with pgvector. They also describe vector indexes for approximate nearest neighbor search, explicitly aimed at similarity search over machine-learning embeddings. Both storage and search happen inside the database, with no separate vector store. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration, and documented detail on distance metrics, dimension limits and query syntax.

support.subject: As a developer, I can store embeddings and run vector similarity search natively without adding a separate vector database

citations.quote: A _vector index_ enables efficient approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search on high-dimensional columns.
`VECTOR` functionality is compatible with the [`pgvector`](https://github.com/pgvector/pgvector) extension for PostgreSQL.
Use vector indexes to improve the performance of similarity searches over large datasets, such as embeddings generated by machine learning models.
